messages:
nora (partnerships): heads-up from billing: GSI reported a shortfall vs their invoice for last-month marketplace consumption. they see ~18% less than expected. can partnerships + eng look? :mag:

rajesh (gsi-partner): sending sample merged payload we push from our aggregator. we merge device-level usage into a single event per customer/day. maybe the merge lost duplicate keys. sample below.

rajesh (gsi-partner): ```
{customer_id: "acme-corp", day: "2024-09-14", usage_entries: 3, total_units: 12400, merge_key: "acme-20240914"}
```

nora (partnerships): quick Q 1: do we expect raw events or pre-merged daily totals from GSIs? our marketplace contract says hourly granularity preferred but allows daily rollups if signed off.

rajesh (gsi-partner): we negotiated daily rollups to reduce chattiness. doc reference in onboarding portal. maybe our merge_key collisions triggered dedup in your ingestion.

cal (billing): downstream we dedupe on partner_event_id + partner_source. if merge_key == partner_event_id and two different merge processes used same id, one could be dropped. that would undercount.

tess (eng-recon): looking at ingestion logs: for contract gsi-enterprise-9 we saw repeated ACKs for partner_event_id "acme-20240914" with different total_units. latest write wins, earlier totals replaced. GSI sent incremental merges (first 9k then corrected to 12.4k) but our pipeline treated them as idempotent and ignored updates.

nora (partnerships): so partner sent corrections but pipeline only accepts first seen. we need to accept deltas or accept updates. which is easier?

tess (eng-recon): two paths: 1) quick change: allow updates for events within a 7-day window by upserting on partner_event_id and emit reconciliation delta events; 2) longer: require partner to send monotonic sequence numbers and an explicit 'final=true' flag. path 1 is faster.

partners-bot: created ticket PART-5710 (gsi-merge-upsert) assigned to tess.
